section_summary.extract_value: This section reports measurement invariance testing across sex and ethnicity for the Body Appreciation Scale-2 (BAS-2) in a sample of 781 participants (with 471 included in the ANOVA). The study found partial scalar invariance for both sex and ethnicity comparisons. A 2×2 ANOVA revealed no significant sex effect or sex-by-ethnicity interaction, but a significant main effect of ethnicity, with Malay participants showing significantly higher body appreciation than Chinese participants. Table 3 presents correlations between body appreciation and additional measures (satisfaction with life, subjective happiness, drive for muscularity, actual-ideal weight discrepancy, pressure and internalization, information, and body mass index) separately for women (upper diagonal) and men (lower diagonal).
